# dsh-project-memory
**Languages:** English · 简体中文 · 日本語 · Español

Project memory for DeepSeek Harness: your documents, your
development state, and durable memory atom

s that survive restarts and context compaction.
A host-only cordis plugin, plus one sidebar panel.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## The problem

An agent starts every session blank. So you re-explain the structure, it re-reads the same
documents

, it re-makes a decision you settled last week, and it repeats a mistake it
already hit.

Inside one session the same thing happens more quietly. When the context gets long the
harness compa

cts it: the original turns are replaced by a summary. Context stays
affordable, and everything the s
ummary left out is gone for good.

This plugin gives the project a memory stored **in the repository**, not in a context
window.
## How it works

Three stores, because what you *wrote*, what you *are doing*, and what you *decided* have
different

es, because what you *wrote*, what you *are doing*, and what you *decided* have
different lifetimes:
| system | holds | written by | survives |

| **A — documents** | your Markdown | you, in git | everything |
| **B — state** | task, progress, b

lockers, decisions | `state_update` / `state_handoff` | restarts, compaction |
| **C — atoms** | sho
rt durable statements | the compaction observer, `memory_remember` | restarts, compaction |
The interesting one is **C**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Four properties make it cheap enough to run on every step:

1. **Sparse, not dumped.** A handful of atoms out of hundreds, ranked for *this* request.
A hard tok

en ceiling means cost is set by configuration, not by project size.
2. **Recorded, not scraped.** St

ate and atoms are written by tool calls. An agent that
never calls `state_update` gets no state memo

ry — a visible failure instead of a quietly
wrong one. The one deliberate exception: the compaction

observer reads compaction
summaries, which is exactly what system C exists to rescue.
3. **Rules out

rank relevance.** A `constraint` atom is *standing*: it is selected before
any scoring runs and kept

even when the request's wording does not match it. A rule
that only applies when you happen to ment

ion it is not a rule.
4. **Selection never writes.** The optional router subagent may only answer wi

th ids that
were offered to it; an id it invents is discarded. Mutation stays in deterministic code.
### Router tiers
| `routerTier` | behaviour | cost |

| `off` | deterministic gating only | free |
| `smart` (default) | escalates only when the determini

stic pass found nothing relevant or matched weakly | free until a provider **and** model are set |
|
`always` | every step asks the router | one call per step |

`smart` costs nothing out of the box: it needs both `routerProvider` and `routerModel`.
`routerStrat

egy` (`task` / `compliance` / `orient`) changes the instructions the router
receives, so two profile
s with the same atoms can still recall differently.
### Standing is not weight

Weight (1–5) is a *ranking* input. Standing is an *eligibility* input, decided by kind
(`constraint`

), never by weight. Fusing them was a real bug: genuine rules stored at the
default weight silently

lost their hard-rule status. Standing atoms still obey the count
and token caps — a budget share, no

-rule status. Standing atoms still obey the count
and token caps — a budget share, not an exemption.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The manifest declares `dsh.bundle`, so one command adds the dependency **and** the bundle
entry:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Restart the host, then call `project_inspect`: a resolved project root and an indexed
document count

then call `project_inspect`: a resolved project root and an indexed
document count mean it is live.
[该节后续省略]
## What is measured, and what is not

**Measured** (`docs/design/benchmark-compaction-loss.md`): on 80 questions from a real
dataset, summ

ary-only and tail-only contexts scored 16.3% and 15.0% correct; summary plus
atom recall scored 25.0

%. Every confidence interval crosses zero, so this is a consistent
direction, **not an established e

confidence interval crosses zero, so this is a consistent
direction, **not an established effect**.
**Not measured**:

- **Router accuracy — zero.** The router subagent has never run against a live model. Its
tests cove

r timeout, abort, malformed replies and unknown ids with a stubbed delegate;
no real spawn has been

observed producing a real selection. Its `smart` trigger rate is
likewise unmeasured: the escalation

rules are in `decideRoute`, the frequency with which
they fire is not.
- **Cost of a full scan.** `

gateAtoms` scores every live atom on every recall
(`core/gate.js`). Measured here — 401-record store

, this machine — one `readAtoms` costs
≈ 5.6 ms and one `gateAtoms` ≈ 9.4 ms; on uniform synthetic a

toms the gate grows
roughly linearly at ≈ 0.7 / 1.0 / 1.6 / 3.3 ms for 100 / 200 / 400 / 800 atoms.

No
inverted index exists. Standing selection is a separate *pass*, but it reuses the same scan, so
i

t is not an independent candidate channel.
- **Parsing cost of `atoms.jsonl`.** Every recall re-read

s and re-parses the whole file
(`lib/recall.js`); there is no in-process snapshot cache. Any cache n

eeds cross-process
invalidation (another session, another process, or `memory_forget` can rewrite th

e file),
which is why it is a design item rather than a patch.

Search is lexical, not semantic. The router degrades to deterministic selection on timeout,
so its w
orst case is a missed improvement, not a broken step.
## What it will not do

- It will not modify `AGENTS.md`, `docs/decisions/`, `docs/adr/`, or `.git/`. `docs_sync`
refuses th

ose paths and names the refusal.
- It will not commit, branch, or push. It records git facts; it doe

s not perform git work.
- It will not silently invent state. Every write is compare-and-set; concurr

ent writes
conflict instead of overwriting.
- It will not rewrite an authoritative document. Proposa
ls go to `docs/proposals/`.
